warnings: Avoid spraying into the eyes, which may cause blurred vision or eye pain. It works more slowly than salbutamol. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Other anticholinergic medicines (some antihistamines, antidepressants) can add to dry mouth and urinary problems. Using with other bronchodilators is usually intended. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Tiotropium is an inhaled once-daily medicine that keeps the airways open for 24 hours. It is mainly used in chronic obstructive lung disease and as an add-on in difficult asthma. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Dry mouth, constipation, throat irritation, urinary difficulty, sinus infection. Rarely: fast heartbeat, narrow-angle glaucoma worsening. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to tiotropium or atropine-like medicines. Use carefully with glaucoma, enlarged prostate and severe kidney disease. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Not for sudden breathlessness. Avoid getting the powder in the eyes. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Other anticholinergic medicines can add to dry mouth, constipation and urinary problems. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Fexofenadine is a non-sedating antihistamine for hay fever, sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes and itchy hives. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, mild drowsiness, nausea, dizziness. Rarely: allergic reactions. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to fexofenadine. Doses are lowered in kidney disease. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Do not take it with fruit juice (apple, orange or grapefruit), which can reduce absorption; take with water. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium reduce its absorption; take them at least 2 hours apart. Erythromycin and ketoconazole can raise its levels. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Levocetirizine relieves allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itchy skin rashes. It is usually taken once a day at night. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, tiredness, headache. Rarely: weight gain or urinary difficulty. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in severe kidney disease or if allergic to it or to cetirizine. Not for people with certain rare urinary retention problems. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: May cause sleepiness, so take with caution before driving. Doses need to be lowered in kidney disease and in older adults. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Alcohol and sedatives increase drowsiness. Theophylline may slightly reduce its clearance. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Loratadine is a low-sedation antihistamine for hay fever and other allergies, taken once daily. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, dry mouth, tiredness, mild drowsiness, stomach upset. Rarely: palpitations. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to loratadine. Reduce dose in severe liver disease. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Less sleepy than older antihistamines, but still be careful when driving. Stop if rash or swelling of the face occurs. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Ketoconazole, erythromycin and cimetidine can raise its levels. Alcohol may slightly add to drowsiness. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; GINA guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Omeprazole sharply reduces the amount of acid the stomach makes. It treats heartburn, acid reflux, gastritis and stomach ulcers and is taken before a meal. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, stomach pain, diarrhea, nausea, gas, constipation. Long-term use may lower vitamin B12 and magnesium levels and slightly raise fracture risk. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to omeprazole or similar PPIs. Not with rilpivirine. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Use the lowest dose for the shortest time that works. Long-term use needs a doctor's review. See a doctor if you have trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools or unexplained weight loss. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Can reduce the effect of clopidogrel (blood-clot preventer). May raise levels of phenytoin and warfarin, lower absorption of iron, ketoconazole and atazanavir, and interact with methotrexate. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Pantoprazole lowers stomach acid and is used for acid reflux, gastritis, ulcers and protection of the stomach in people taking painkillers. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, diarrhea, nausea, gas, dizziness. Long-term: low magnesium, low vitamin B12, bone fracture risk. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to pantoprazole or other PPIs. Not with rilpivirine. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Take 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast. Needs periodic review if used for more than a few weeks. Report black stools, severe diarrhea or difficulty swallowing. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Less likely than omeprazole to interfere with clopidogrel. May lower absorption of ketoconazole, iron and some HIV medicines, and may raise methotrexate levels. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Esomeprazole is a PPI that strongly reduces stomach acid, used for reflux disease, healing damaged food pipe and ulcers. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, stomach pain, diarrhea, nausea, gas. Long term: low magnesium and vitamin B12, fracture risk. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to PPIs. Not with rilpivirine. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Use the shortest effective course. Persistent symptoms need medical review. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Can reduce the effect of clopidogrel. May change levels of diazepam, phenytoin and warfarin and lower absorption of iron and ketoconazole. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Rabeprazole reduces stomach acid quickly and is used for reflux, gastritis, ulcers and as part of treatment for Helicobacter pylori infection. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, dizziness. Long term: low magnesium and vitamin B12. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to PPIs. Not with rilpivirine. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Swallow the tablet whole. Long-term use needs monitoring. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: May reduce absorption of ketoconazole and iron. Can raise digoxin and methotrexate levels slightly. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Lansoprazole reduces stomach acid and treats reflux, gastritis and ulcers. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, diarrhea, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain. Long-term: low magnesium and B12. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to PPIs. Not with rilpivirine. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Take 30 minutes before a meal. See a doctor if symptoms continue beyond 2 weeks of treatment. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: May reduce absorption of ketoconazole, iron and some HIV medicines. Theophylline levels may fall slightly; tacrolimus levels may rise. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Famotidine reduces stomach acid by blocking histamine receptors in the stomach. It relieves heartburn and acidity and can be taken as needed or at night. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, constipation or diarrhea. Rarely: confusion, especially in the elderly and in kidney disease. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to famotidine or other H2 blockers. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Reduce the dose in kidney disease. Antacids and food can affect how it works. See a doctor if heartburn is frequent. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: May lower absorption of ketoconazole, itraconazole and some HIV medicines (such as atazanavir). Antacids can slightly reduce its absorption. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Domperidone speeds up emptying of the stomach and eases nausea, bloating and the feeling of fullness. It is also used with reflux symptoms. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Dry mouth, headache, diarrhea, cramps, breast tenderness. Serious but rare: dangerous heart rhythm changes (QT prolongation). (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in heart rhythm problems, heart failure, severe liver disease, bleeding or blockage in the gut, and with ketoconazole, erythromycin or other drugs that strongly raise its level. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Use the lowest dose for the shortest time (not more than 1 week for most nausea). Take before meals. Stop and seek help if you have palpitations or fainting. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin and fluconazole raise its level and the heart rhythm risk. Other QT-prolonging medicines, such as ondansetron or some antipsychotics, add to the risk. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Sucralfate forms a protective layer over ulcers and inflamed areas of the stomach and gut so that they can heal. It does not reduce stomach acid. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Constipation, dry mouth, nausea, indigestion, rash. Rarely: high aluminium levels in kidney failure. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in severe kidney failure and in people allergic to sucralfate. Use with caution in diabetes. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Take on an empty stomach, an hour before meals and at bedtime. It can stick to other medicines, so separate it from them by at least 2 hours. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Reduces absorption of ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, tetracyclines, warfarin, digoxin, levothyroxine, phenytoin and many others. Antacids reduce its effect. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: This antacid combination neutralises stomach acid and gives fast but short-lasting relief from heartburn and sour stomach. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Constipation (aluminium) or loose stools (magnesium), chalky taste, mild stomach upset. High levels of aluminium or magnesium may build up in kidney failure. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid or use only on medical advice in severe kidney disease. Not for long-term daily use without advice. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Take after meals and at bedtime. Space it at least 2 hours from other medicines. Seek advice if you need antacids for more than 2 weeks. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Reduces absorption of many medicines, including ciprofloxacin, tetracyclines, iron, levothyroxine, digoxin and some HIV medicines. Take other medicines 2 hours before or after. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Sodium alginate forms a gel layer on top of the stomach contents after a meal, which blocks acid from flowing back into the food pipe. It is usually taken after meals and at bedtime. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Generally well tolerated. Occasional bloating, nausea, diarrhea or constipation. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to any ingredient. Check for the sodium and calcium content in people with high blood pressure, heart or kidney disease. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Contains sodium; people on salt-restricted diets should check the label. Not a substitute for acid-reducing medicine if symptoms are frequent. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Can reduce absorption of other medicines if taken together; separate by about 2 hours. Antacid-containing forms share antacid interactions. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Itopride helps the stomach empty faster and eases bloating, fullness and nausea (functional dyspepsia). It is taken before meals. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Diarrhea, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness. Rarely: raised prolactin with breast tenderness. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in stomach bleeding, perforation or blockage of the gut, and if allergic to itopride. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: May cause dizziness. Use with care in the elderly and in kidney or liver disease. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Anticholinergic medicines (such as dicyclomine or some antihistamines) can reduce its effect. (Source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: FDA/EMA labels; ACG guidelines; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Chloroquine treats malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax in areas where it still works. It is not suitable where the parasite is resistant, which is common for falciparum malaria. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Nausea, stomach upset, headache, itching, dizziness, blurred vision. Rarely: heart rhythm changes, retina damage with long use. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to chloroquine, or with existing retina disease. Use with care in heart rhythm problems, liver disease, seizures and psoriasis. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Take with food to reduce stomach upset. Prolonged use needs eye checks. Treatment must be taken for the full course. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Antacids and kaolin reduce absorption; separate by 4 hours. Other QT-prolonging medicines, such as amiodarone and some antibiotics, raise heart rhythm risk. Cimetidine raises its levels. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Primaquine clears the dormant liver forms of P. vivax and P. ovale parasites so that malaria does not come back, and reduces spread of falciparum malaria. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite. Serious: breakdown of red blood cells in people with G6PD deficiency. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in G6PD deficiency (unless under supervision), in pregnancy, in infants under 6 months, and in people with severe blood disease. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: A G6PD test is advised before use. Stop at once and see a doctor if urine turns dark, or if you become pale, tired or breathless. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Other medicines that can damage the blood or cause hemolysis in G6PD deficiency (such as dapsone and sulfonamides) add to the risk. Quinacrine increases its toxicity. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Artemether-lumefantrine is a first-line combination for uncomplicated falciparum malaria. The artemether kills parasites quickly and the lumefantrine clears the rest. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, loss of appetite, weakness, joint and muscle pain, stomach upset. Rarely: heart rhythm changes. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in severe malaria, in people with heart rhythm problems or a long QT interval, and if allergic to its components. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Take with a fatty meal or milk to improve absorption, and complete all 6 doses over 3 days. Avoid grapefruit juice. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Rifampicin, carbamazepine and phenytoin lower its effect. Ketoconazole, ritonavir and QT-prolonging drugs raise the risk of heart rhythm problems. It can reduce hormonal contraceptive effect. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Artesunate is a fast-acting antimalarial given by injection for severe malaria, or by mouth with another medicine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Dizziness, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache. Delayed breakdown of red blood cells can occur one to three weeks after treatment. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to artemisinins. Use with care in the first trimester of pregnancy unless it is the only available option for severe malaria. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Blood tests are advised for about a month after severe malaria treatment because of delayed anaemia. Never use as a single medicine for long. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Few important interactions. Medicines that damage the liver may add to side effects. Enzyme inducers like rifampicin can lower its effect. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine is used together with artesunate in a combination treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in parts of India. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, rash, itching, headache. Rare but serious: severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), blood disorders, liver injury. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to sulfa drugs, in infants under 2 months, in severe kidney or liver disease, and in anaemia due to folate deficiency. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Stop at the first sign of rash or mouth sores. Not for prolonged use. Not suitable where resistance is high. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Co-trimoxazole and other folate-blocking medicines add to toxicity. Folic acid supplements can reduce its effect. Phenytoin and rifampicin interact. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Quinine treats severe or drug-resistant malaria and is used when artemisinin-based options are not available, often with doxycycline. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Ringing in the ears, headache, nausea, blurred vision, dizziness (cinchonism). Low blood sugar, heart rhythm changes, and rare blood disorders. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in people with heart rhythm problems, a long QT interval, optic neuritis, G6PD deficiency or myasthenia gravis, and if allergic to quinine. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Can cause dangerously low blood sugar, especially in pregnancy and children. Take with food. Overdose is dangerous. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: QT-prolonging medicines (such as macrolides, fluoroquinolones, domperidone) increase heart risk. It raises digoxin levels and can interact with warfarin. Antacids reduce absorption. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: In malaria, doxycycline is combined with quinine or artesunate to improve cure, and is also used for malaria prevention. It is an antibiotic with many other uses. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Nausea, stomach upset, sun sensitivity, throat irritation or ulcers. Rarely: liver injury, headache with raised pressure inside the skull. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy, breastfeeding and in children under 8 years because it can affect teeth and bones. Avoid if allergic to tetracyclines. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Take with a full glass of water and stay upright for 30 minutes to protect the food pipe. Use sun protection. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Antacids, iron, calcium and zinc supplements, and dairy reduce its absorption; separate by 2 to 3 hours. Rifampicin, phenytoin and carbamazepine lower its levels. It may strengthen warfarin. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Mefloquine is used for treatment and prevention of malaria, mainly in areas with chloroquine resistance. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Dizziness, nausea, vivid dreams, headache, sleep problems, anxiety. Serious: psychiatric symptoms, seizures, balance problems that may persist. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in people with a history of depression, psychosis, seizures or other psychiatric disorders, and in people with heart rhythm problems. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Stop and contact a doctor if you develop anxiety, depression, restlessness, confusion or balance problems. Take with food. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Quinine, quinidine and other QT-prolonging medicines raise heart risk. Antiepileptic medicines may be less effective. Rifampicin lowers its levels. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Atovaquone-proguanil is used to treat uncomplicated falciparum malaria and to prevent malaria in travellers. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, cough. Rare: raised liver enzymes and mouth ulcers. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in severe kidney disease for prevention, and if allergic to its ingredients. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Take with food or milk at the same time daily. If you vomit within an hour of a dose, take another dose and seek advice. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Rifampicin and tetracycline reduce its levels. Metoclopramide may reduce atovaquone absorption. It can raise warfarin effect. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Tafenoquine is a single-dose medicine that prevents relapse of vivax malaria, used after the blood stage has been treated. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Headache, dizziness, nausea, back pain, high blood methaemoglobin, sleep problems. Serious: hemolysis in G6PD deficiency and psychiatric symptoms. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Must not be used in G6PD deficiency, in pregnancy, in breastfeeding where the infant is G6PD deficient or untested, or in people with psychotic illness. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: A G6PD test is mandatory before use. Report any mood or psychiatric changes. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Drugs that cause hemolysis or affect organic cation transport (such as metformin, dofetilide) may interact. Use other antimalarials only as advised. (Source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: WHO Guidelines for Malaria; NCVBDC India malaria guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

active_ingredient: Sodium Chloride; Potassium Chloride; Calcium Chloride; Sodium Lactate
description: Dengue has no specific antiviral medicine; treatment is supportive. Ringer's lactate is an intravenous fluid used to replace lost fluid and keep blood pressure stable when a patient with dengue cannot drink enough or shows warning signs. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Fluid overload (swelling, breathlessness), if given too much or too fast. Rarely: high potassium or injection-site irritation. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in severe liver failure, high blood potassium, high blood lactate, and in fluid overload or heart failure unless closely monitored. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Given only under medical supervision with careful monitoring of fluid balance, because both too little and too much fluid are harmful in dengue. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Mixing with some injected medicines (such as ceftriaxone) can form precipitates. Potassium-sparing diuretics and ACE inhibitors raise potassium risk. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Normal saline is an intravenous fluid used in supportive care of dengue to replace fluid lost from the blood vessels when there are warning signs or dehydration. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Fluid overload, swelling, breathlessness, raised sodium and chloride levels if given in excess. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid or use with caution in heart failure, severe kidney disease, high blood sodium and swelling. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Fluid is adjusted carefully by a doctor with monitoring of blood pressure, urine output and hematocrit. Over-hydration can cause lung congestion. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Corticosteroids and some anti-inflammatory medicines can increase sodium and fluid retention. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Dextrose saline is an intravenous fluid that provides fluid, salt and a small amount of sugar. In dengue it is used as maintenance fluid for patients who cannot eat or drink adequately, as directed by a doctor. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: High blood sugar, low sodium, swelling, fluid overload, irritation at the injection site. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid or use cautiously in uncontrolled diabetes, severe kidney or heart failure, and low sodium levels. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Blood sugar and electrolytes should be monitored, especially in people with diabetes. It must not be given as the only fluid for resuscitation. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Corticosteroids and diuretics change sugar and electrolyte balance. Insulin dose may need adjusting in people with diabetes. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Ondansetron controls vomiting and nausea, including the persistent vomiting seen with dengue, gastroenteritis and after surgery or chemotherapy. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Headache, constipation, tiredness, dizziness. Rarely: heart rhythm changes (QT prolongation). (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in congenital long QT syndrome and with apomorphine. Use carefully in liver disease, electrolyte imbalance and heart rhythm problems. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Report palpitations or fainting. It treats vomiting only and does not treat the underlying illness; persistent vomiting in dengue needs medical review. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: QT-prolonging medicines (domperidone, macrolides, quinine, some antipsychotics) increase heart risk. Serotonin-raising medicines can cause serotonin syndrome. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

description: Metoclopramide stops nausea and vomiting and speeds up stomach emptying. It is used for short-term relief of vomiting. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
side_effects: Drowsiness, restlessness, tiredness, diarrhea. Serious: involuntary muscle movements (tardive dyskinesia), muscle spasms, especially in children and the young. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
contraindications: Avoid in gut bleeding, obstruction or perforation, epilepsy, phaeochromocytoma, Parkinson's disease, and in young children. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
warnings: Use for no more than 5 days. Long-term use can cause permanent movement disorders. Reduce the dose in kidney disease. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
major_interactions: Antipsychotics and other dopamine-blocking medicines add to movement disorder risk. Sedatives and alcohol increase drowsiness. Opioids and anticholinergics oppose its effect. (Source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels)
source: NCVBDC/NVBDCP India dengue guidelines; WHO dengue guidelines; FDA/EMA labels

active_ingredient: Sodium Chloride; Glucose; Potassium Chloride; Sodium Citrate
description: ORS replaces the water and salts lost in diarrhea and vomiting and is the most important treatment for most cases of gastroenteritis, especially in children and the elderly. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Vomiting if taken too quickly; swelling of the eyelids or face with excessive intake. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in intestinal blockage, paralysed gut, severe dehydration with shock (needs a drip), and in people who cannot drink. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Mix exactly as directed in clean (boiled and cooled) water; do not add sugar or salt. Give small sips often. Seek medical help if there is blood in stool, high fever, or signs of severe dehydration. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: No major drug interactions. Do not mix with juices or soft drinks. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Zinc given for 10 to 14 days during diarrhea in children shortens the illness and lowers the chance of the diarrhea returning in the next few months. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, metallic taste. Long use of high doses can cause copper deficiency. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to zinc products. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Complete the full course even after loose motions stop. Take with food if it causes stomach upset. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Reduces absorption of quinolone antibiotics (ciprofloxacin), tetracyclines and penicillamine; separate by 2 to 3 hours. Iron and calcium supplements may compete with it. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Racecadotril reduces the amount of water and salts the gut releases during diarrhea, without slowing the gut. It is used with ORS for acute watery diarrhea. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Headache, mild rash. Rarely: swelling of the face or lips (angioedema), serious skin reactions. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to it, in blood or mucus in stool, in diarrhea due to antibiotics, and in severe kidney or liver disease. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Does not replace rehydration. Stop and seek help if a rash or swelling develops. Not for bloody or very high-fever diarrhea. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: ACE inhibitors (such as enalapril and ramipril) increase the risk of angioedema. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Loperamide slows the movement of the gut so that stools become firmer and less frequent. It gives short-term relief from watery diarrhea in adults. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Constipation, abdominal cramps, bloating, dizziness, nausea, dry mouth. Very high doses can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in blood in stool, high fever, bacterial or antibiotic-related colitis, bowel blockage, and in children under 2 years. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Do not use if you have fever or blood in stool. Stop if there is no improvement in 48 hours. Never exceed the maximum dose. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Quinidine, ritonavir and gemfibrozil raise loperamide levels. Other QT-prolonging medicines add to heart risk. Other constipating medicines may add to its effect. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Metronidazole treats diarrhea caused by amoebae and giardia and some bacterial infections of the gut. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Metallic taste, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache, dark urine. Rarely: numbness or tingling in hands and feet, seizures. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in the first trimester of pregnancy unless needed, and if allergic to nitroimidazoles. Avoid with disulfiram. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Do not drink alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours afterwards; it can cause flushing, vomiting and palpitations. Complete the course as directed. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Alcohol, disulfiram and lithium interactions. It strengthens the effect of warfarin. Phenytoin and phenobarbital lower its levels. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Tinidazole is used for giardiasis, amoebic dysentery and other gut parasite infections, often as a single or short course. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Metallic taste, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, dark urine, dizziness. Rare: nerve problems and seizures. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in the first trimester of pregnancy, in blood disorders, and if allergic to nitroimidazoles. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Do not drink alcohol during treatment and for 3 days afterwards. Take with food. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Alcohol and disulfiram cause severe reactions. It can raise the effect of warfarin and lithium. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic used for severe bacterial diarrhea, including traveller's diarrhea and dysentery, when a doctor decides it is needed. Most watery diarrhea does not need antibiotics. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, rash, sun sensitivity. Serious: tendon pain or rupture, nerve damage, mood changes, heart rhythm changes. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in people with a history of tendon problems with quinolones, in myasthenia gravis, during pregnancy and in children unless specifically needed, and with tizanidine. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Stop and see a doctor if you have tendon, joint or muscle pain, or tingling in the hands or feet. Avoid strenuous exercise during treatment. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Tizanidine must not be combined. Antacids, iron, calcium and zinc reduce absorption. It raises theophylline and caffeine levels, enhances warfarin and may cause seizures with NSAIDs. QT-prolonging medicines add heart risk. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Norfloxacin is an antibiotic sometimes used for bacterial gut and urinary infections when a doctor considers it necessary. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Nausea, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, sleep problems. Serious: tendon injury, nerve damage and mood changes. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in tendon problems with quinolones, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy, and in children, and if allergic to quinolones. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Stop at once if tendon pain, swelling or tingling occurs. Not for ordinary watery diarrhea. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Antacids, iron, zinc and calcium reduce absorption. May increase theophylline and warfarin effects; NSAIDs raise seizure risk. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Azithromycin is an antibiotic used for certain bacterial diarrhea (such as some typhoid-type and traveller's diarrhea) and for children where fluoroquinolones are unsuitable. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, vomiting. Rarely: liver problems, hearing changes, heart rhythm changes. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to macrolides and in people with long QT syndrome or significant heart rhythm problems. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Report palpitations, fainting, severe diarrhea or yellowing of eyes or skin. Complete the full course. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Antacids with aluminium or magnesium reduce absorption. QT-prolonging medicines (domperidone, ondansetron, quinine) add heart risk. It can raise warfarin effects. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Nitazoxanide treats diarrhea caused by parasites such as Giardia and Cryptosporidium. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Stomach pain, nausea, headache, diarrhea. Urine may turn yellow-green, which is harmless. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid if allergic to nitazoxanide. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Take with food. Use with caution in liver or kidney disease. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: May increase the effect of warfarin and other highly protein-bound drugs. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: This probiotic yeast helps restore healthy gut flora, and reduces the duration of acute diarrhea and diarrhea linked to antibiotics. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Gas, bloating, constipation, thirst. Rarely: infection in severely ill or immunocompromised people. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in people with a central venous catheter, severe illness, weakened immunity or yeast allergy. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: Do not mix with very hot food or drinks, or alcohol. Seek help if fever develops. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Antifungal medicines can reduce its effect. Not recommended with other live organisms in immunosuppressed patients. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022

description: Dicyclomine relaxes the gut muscle and relieves cramping pain and colic that go with diarrhea and irritable bowel conditions. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
side_effects: Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, drowsiness, fast heartbeat, difficulty passing urine. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
contraindications: Avoid in glaucoma, bowel obstruction, severe ulcerative colitis, enlarged prostate with urine retention, myasthenia gravis, and in infants under 6 months. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
warnings: May cause drowsiness and blurred vision. Not for diarrhea with high fever or bloody stools. Use caution in the elderly and in hot weather (heat stroke risk). (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
major_interactions: Antihistamines, tricyclic antidepressants, antipsychotics and other anticholinergics add to dry mouth, confusion and constipation. Antacids reduce its absorption. (Source: WHO/ICMR diarrhoea guidelines; FDA/EMA labels; WHO EML; NLEM India 2022)
